steps.message:
Before I write anything: this is a destructive, one-way change, so I want an explicit go-ahead.

`migrations/003` would run `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` against production, where the README says `users` has 48,000 rows. Whatever text is in `notes` for those rows is permanently gone once the deploy job applies it — there's no down-migration that brings it back, and a restore would mean a full database rollback. "We stopped using it" tells me no code reads it; it doesn't tell me nobody would want the contents later (support history, manual annotations, etc.).

questions.question: Dropping `notes` permanently deletes that data for all 48,000 production rows. How should I proceed?

options.label: Archive, then drop
options.description: Migration 003 copies id + notes into a users_notes_archive table (only for non-null notes), then drops the column. Data is recoverable; one extra table sticks around.

options.label: Just drop it
options.description: Migration 003 is a single ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes, plus the matching edit to schema.sql. Data is unrecoverable after deploy.

options.label: Hold off
options.description: I write nothing until you've checked whether anything still depends on the notes contents.

steps.message:
Done.

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — new, single `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line so the mirror stays in sync (the README says it's maintained by hand)

Two things to be aware of before this deploys:

- `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35.0 or newer (March 2021). On older versions the migration fails with a syntax error and the deploy job stops there. Worth a quick check of the production SQLite version if you don't already know it.
- No down-migration exists, matching the existing 001/002 style. Nothing ran against a database — I didn't apply or test the migration.
